title: Check yourself: Latency, throughput, region and cost budgets, and the architecture that fits

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A feature must label two million archived tickets overnight, and nobody reads the labels until morning. The team proposes a pool of workers that call the API one ticket at a time all night. Which change fits the requirement best?

options.text: Stream every reply from the workers so that the first words of each label arrive sooner
options.says: Ruled out because streaming "does not shorten the total time", and no reader is watching the words arrive.

options.text: Hand the whole job to the batch interface, which halves the price and runs unattended
options.says: Nobody is waiting and volume is large, which the page assigns to a batch: "most batches finishing in less than 1 hour while reducing costs by 50%".

options.text: Move the workers to the fastest tier so that the overnight window is certain to be enough
options.says: Ruled out because a faster tier is correct only "if your evaluation set (page 1) says its quality holds", and it does not change the cost.

options.text: Chain a second call after each label that checks the label before the result is stored
options.says: Ruled out because "chaining calls multiplies latency" and also cost, and the requirement gives no reason for a second call.

questions.stem: A requirement says customer data may only be processed in the United States. A developer plans to use `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` and set `inference_geo` to `"us"` on every request. What does the page predict?

options.text: The calls succeed and are billed at 1.1 times the standard rate for inference kept in the US
options.says: Ruled out because the 1.1 times price belongs to models where the setting is "supported on Claude 4.6 and later", which excludes this one.

options.text: The calls succeed and run in any region, because the unsupported setting is quietly dropped
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation says such requests "return a 400 error", so the setting is rejected and not dropped.

options.text: The calls fail with a 429 error, because the capacity inside the US for that model is limited
options.says: Ruled out because "Rate limits are shared across all geos", so the setting opens no separate US pool whose capacity could run out.

options.text: The calls fail with a 400 error, because the setting is not supported on that model
options.says: The page says a request that sets the geography on Claude Haiku 4.5 or an earlier model "return a 400 error".
